doc.title: Eiji Kitamura interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999

title: His Yamaha clarinet model
summary: He praises Yamaha instruments for their flexible tone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I see you have a clarinet model named after you? Is that right? With Yamaha?

Yes. I like Yamaha instruments. It’s very good for me because Yamaha has many different tone colors it can make. Selmer or Buffet Crampon has its own tone color. But Yamaha has many tones. If I play only the same instrument, the same mouthpiece, the same reed, I can play classic and jazz and Dixieland, any kind is okay.
It’s more flexible, yeah. Excellent. Well you’re a good spokesman for the company. I’m sure they’re glad that you play their instruments. Do you get to play in New York City?
